newsitem.title: HONG KONG: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks to give China roaring welcome.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD-HK stocks to give China roaring welcome.

text.p: The Hong Kong stock market is braced to give Britain a roaring sendoff during the final week of colonial rule, welcoming its prospects under China with a record-breaking rally, analysts said.

The blue chip Hang Seng Index will enter this coming week in record ground, after staging its biggest point gain on Friday with a rise of 647.87 points, or 4.47 percent, to an all-time high of 15,154.36 points.
"It is certainly linked to the handover," said Howard Gorges, vice chairman at South China Holdings. "The momentum we have got suggests there could be some follow-through."
Hong Kong returns to Chinese rule on midnight of June 30.
Prospects of further economic integration between Hong Kong and China have boosted investor sentiment in the territory, sending share prices to record highs.

"If this is a sentiment-driven rally, then you would expect that sentiment would want to see the index at an all-time high around the handover," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading at CS First Boston.
Analysts said the Hang Seng Index could forge ahead to 15,500 points this coming week.
"It broke through 15,000 on huge volume suggesting that upward momentum could continue for a while," said Alex Tang, head of research at Yamaichi International.
"How much it can go up is anybody's guess now."

A move by China late on Friday to tighten its grip on red chip companies could dampen sentiment in the red chip sector, but analysts said the move had been largely discounted by the market and would ultimately lead to a healthier environment.

China said on Friday that Chinese-controlled companies making share offers abroad must obtain approval from domestic regulators and government approval would be required for asset transfers to Chinese-controlled companies abroad if the purpose was to inject the assets into a listed vehicle.
"It makes red chips a little less attractive," said Kent Rossiter, institutional sales manager at Nikko Securities.
But he said demand for red chips would remain strong and the overall market should not suffer too much from the announcement.
"With the way it ended on Friday which was incredible, I would say it looks, despite this news on red chips, like the index will be seeing higher territory," said Rossiter.

Analysts said sentiment could turn more cautious as stocks scale higher, prompting some profit-taking by mid-week. Property stocks, which rallied late last week on hopes that Hong Kong's new government would avoid imposing draconian measures to curb rising property prices, could see some selling. A government move is widely expected soon after the change in sovereignty.
"No one knows what the measures will be so they might run into profit-taking next week," said Gorges.
Hong Kong will also mark the handover with a three-day holiday for the market, with trade resuming on Thursday July 3.

"There is a U.S. Federal Reserve meeting over the holiday and leaving a lot of money in the market over the long weekend would worry some investors," said Rossiter. The U.S. Federal Reserve is due to meet on July 1 and July 2.
Six initial public offerings will come to the market this coming week, hoping to ride the wave of pre-handover euphoria.

Analysts said the most attractive IPOs were First Tractor Co Ltd's 300 million H-share offering at HK$4.50 per share and Leading Spirit Conrowa Electric Co Ltd's 393 million share offering at HK$1.00. First Tractor is due to make its market debut on Monday and Leading Spirit Conrowa on Thursday.
Wheelock and Co Ltd is due to release its final results on Thursday.
